hero.headline: How messy PDFs became a usable public registry

subhead.text: This page explains the real extraction path in plain language first, then shows the technical proof: scripts, reports, prompts, and iteration checkpoints.

eras.label: Era 1
eras.title: Custom GPT, all PDFs in a knowledge base

system.input: ≈ 1,100 PDFs uploaded to a custom GPT

eras.what: PDFs into a custom GPT's knowledge base, then ask it questions. Zero engineering. Useful as a fuzzy search engine; useless for aggregation. Numbers hallucinated. No audit trail.
why_limited: No way to verify a number, no way to ask 'how do you know'.

artifacts.text: Nothing local survives. The lesson: retrieval over PDFs gives a slightly better search box, not a dataset.

eras.label: Era 2
eras.title: Two deterministic Python scripts
eras.what: Two Python scripts. One pulled rows out of each PDF's tables; the other merged them by natječaj. The whole corpus ran in under an hour with zero LLM cost.
why_good: Cheap — deterministic, no per-PDF API calls.
Got the table-shaped majority. Only ten files in the corpus returned no rows, and they were administrative documents, not funding decisions.
why_limited: Only the tables. Jury rationale — the *why* — was discarded.
No project identity across rounds. The same film in script-dev, production, and distribution showed up as three strangers.
No people. Producer / director / writer were inconsistent or blank.
Amounts locked in without verification. Comma-vs-period decimals and HRK-vs-EUR drifted silently on a long tail of rows.

artifacts.note: Merged per-PDF output into one master CSV, then split by programme
Every file that produced no rows — all admin docs

eras.label: Era 3
eras.title: Pipeline, classifier, ten passes, audit loops

system.output: dataset/master.json · 14 MB · 989 records · 10,388 rows · narratives, people, project identity

what.text: Era 3 split work into two layers: deterministic routing plus LLM extraction/repair passes. Every pass emits an audit artifact, so fixes are explicit instead of hidden.

why_good.text: Traceable chain: PDF -> extraction -> repair report -> updated record.
Failures are inspectable, not silent. Every risky pass left machine-readable evidence.

why_good: Cache layer makes the pipeline restartable. Re-extractions are free.
Captures what Era 2 dropped: jury narratives, people, project identity across rounds, session totals.
Numbers are challenged. The amount-repair pass alone inspected 116 suspect rows and confirmed or fixed 37.

why_limited.text: Expensive in iteration time: many small correction loops over a short window.
Static copy drifts fast unless key numbers are computed from the live dataset.

why_limited: The pipeline assumes HAVC's PDF conventions hold. New layouts need new classifier rules.

artifacts.note: 8 markdown analyses generated on top of the dataset

deep_dive.headline: From intent to dataset, checkpoint by checkpoint

subhead.text: This section shows the operational truth in chronological order: what broke, what was changed, and what evidence remained after each pass.

tally.title: By the numbers
tally.tokens_footnote: Order-of-magnitude estimate. 542 table extractions averaging ~8k input tokens of PDF + ~1.5k tool output ≈ 5.1 M; 418 people-backfill batches × ~7k in + ~1.5k out ≈ 3.6 M; 196 + 240 producer candidates × ~2k tokens ≈ 0.9 M; narrative/decision and Codex audit add ~0.5 M. No hard usage-block tally available in the May session JSONLs.
tally.as_of: Snapshot metrics below: as of 20 May 2026 (report artifacts).

passes.title: Document classifier
passes.engine: havc_pipeline/classify.py · regex over filename + first-page text
passes.what: Every PDF in the corpus first runs through a deterministic classifier that decides where to route it: results_table, narrative, decision, regulation, admin, or non_financing. Pure regex; no LLM. The verdict gates whether a PDF gets a paid extraction.
passes.input: PDF bytes — decoded filename + first-page text dump

io_example.caption: Three real PDFs, three verdicts
io_example.expected:
rezultati MANJINSKE KOPRODUKCIJE - 4. rok 2025.pdf → results_table
obrazlozenje_manjinske_25052016.pdf            → narrative
Pravilnik o provedbi postupka jednostavne nabave 2023.pdf → regulation
io_example.received:
results_table · confidence=high · signals=[fn_results_table, content_amount, content_header]
narrative     · confidence=high · signals=[fn_narrative, content_narrative]
regulation    · confidence=high · signals=[fn_regulation]

metrics.label: Doc types
metrics.note: results_table · narrative · decision · regulation · admin · non_financing

passes.title: Results-table extraction
passes.what: For every PDF classified as results_table, Claude reads it as an image and emits sections + rows via a strict tool schema. The system prompt is the longest and most prescriptive in the pipeline: ten numbered rules covering row capture, diacritics, Croatian decimal convention, HRK/EUR currency, multi-section layouts, column mapping, and how to handle the UKUPNO totals line.
passes.output: { document, sections[ { section_label, columns, rows[ { project_title, production_company, applicant, director, writer, original_author, category, approved_amount_text, approved_amount, currency, extras } ] } ], totals }

prompt_excerpt.caption: havc_pipeline/prompts.py — RESULTS_TABLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, rules 1–4
prompt_excerpt.body:
1. CAPTURE EVERY ROW. Even if a row has missing fields, include it. Never drop a row because the layout is awkward.

2. PRESERVE CROATIAN DIACRITICS exactly: ć, č, š, ž, đ, Ć, Č, Š, Ž, Đ. Never replace them with ?, c, z, etc.

3. AMOUNT FORMAT. Croatian decimal convention uses `.` as thousands separator and `,` as decimal.
   - `19.000,00`   → approved_amount=19000.0
   - `1.234.567,89` → approved_amount=1234567.89
   - `345,00`      → approved_amount=345.0

4. CURRENCY. Croatia adopted the euro on 2023-01-01.
   - Earlier PDFs use kn (Croatian kuna): currency="HRK".
   - Later PDFs use € (euro): currency="EUR".
   - Set both document.currency and per-row currency.

io_example.caption: rezultati komplementarne 2021.pdf — one row through the tool call

passes.title: Narrative + decision extraction
passes.what: Obrazloženja (jury rationale documents) and single-project odluka decisions are prose, not tables. Claude reads them and emits: which call + year + rok the document covers, which project titles are mentioned, and a 1–2 sentence Croatian summary. This is the data behind the dashboard's 'Discussed, never funded' lens.
passes.input: One PDF + classifier verdict = narrative | decision

prompt_excerpt.caption: havc_pipeline/prompts.py — NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_PROMPT
prompt_excerpt.body:
You read short text from HAVC PDFs (Croatian audiovisual centre) and extract metadata. These are either narrative justifications (obrazloženja) by artistic advisors, or decisions (odluke) about funding lists.

Call `emit_narrative_metadata` exactly once with:
- program_type: closest enum match or null if unclear
- year:        4-digit year of the call/decision, or null
- rok:         "N. rok" or null
- referenced_projects: array of project titles mentioned in the text (deduplicated, in order of appearance, exact diacritics preserved)
- summary:     1-2 sentence Croatian summary of what the document says

Preserve Croatian diacritics. Do not invent project titles.

io_example.caption: obrazlozenje_manjinske_25052016.pdf — extracted metadata
io_example.received:
{
  "program_type": "manjinske_koprodukcije",
  "year":         2016,
  "rok":          "2. rok",
  "referenced_projects": ["…12 titles…"],
  "summary":      "Umjetničko vijeće HAVC-a obrazlaže odluku o dodjeli sredstava za manjinske koprodukcije u drugom roku 2016."
}

passes.title: Missing-results backfill
passes.engine: missing-results-backfill extractor channel · re-uses Pass 1's table prompt
passes.what: Some obrazloženja close with a small awarded-projects table; the classifier sent them to narrative, so Pass 1 never saw them. A scan over the dataset surfaces these candidates and re-extracts them with the table prompt, tagged with extractor="missing-results-backfill" so they're distinguishable in master.json. Cached extractions are not re-billed.
passes.input: PDFs flagged by the post-Pass-2 scan as carrying a missed table

prompt_excerpt.caption: Re-uses Pass 1's RESULTS_TABLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT verbatim

io_example.caption: 2013 Razvoj scenarija TV pojedinačna djela.pdf — initially classified narrative
io_example.received:
Pass 3 re-extracts with the table prompt:
  sections: [{ rows: [ { project_title, applicant, approved_amount: …, currency: "HRK" }, … ] }]
  source.extractor: "missing-results-backfill"

passes.title: Drop bogus rows
passes.engine: heuristic Python pass over master.json — no LLM
passes.what: Some extracted rows are clearly not real funding decisions: 'Stavka' placeholder rows leaking from TV development PDFs, HAVC's own postal address parsed as a project title, komplementarne section headers ('filmski festivali i druge audiovizualne manifestacije') that the table parser pulled from a heading row into a project_title cell. A categorical filter tags each with a reason code and removes them.
passes.output: rows minus 139 dropped rows + a report keyed by reason code

prompt_excerpt.caption: Reason codes used by the bogus-row classifier (excerpt)
prompt_excerpt.body:
[stavka_generic_no_amount]   — title is the literal string 'Stavka' with no amount (TV-development placeholder)
[havc_address]               — title contains HAVC's postal address ('Trg Josipa Jurja Strossmayera 4 | 10000 Zagreb | Croatia Tel')
[category_header_bare_count] — title is a komplementarne section header that leaked from a heading row
                                ('filmski festivali i druge audiovizualne manifestacije',
                                 'izdavaštvo u području audiovizualnih djelatnosti',
                                 'programi audiovizualnih udruga i organizacija',
                                 'programi stručnog usavršavanja')

io_example.caption: Three real drops (one per reason code) from _bogus_rows_drop_report.md
io_example.expected: Title looks structurally row-shaped, but is not a project.
io_example.received:
[stavka_generic_no_amount]   RPRSERTV_2021_2rok_9IX2021_WEB.pdf            title='Stavka'                                                  → dropped
[havc_address]               REZULTATI_PRO_VIDEOIGRE_2024.pdf              title='Trg Josipa Jurja Strossmayera 4 | 10000 Zagreb | Croatia Tel' → dropped

passes.title: Amount triage + repair
passes.engine: havc_pipeline/amount_parser.py + Pass A survey + Pass B repair · algorithmic with LLM-assisted neighbourhood inspection
passes.what: The amount parser handles Croatian decimal/thousands conventions, but a long tail of PDFs has OCR drift — '0.000,00' parsed as 0.0, spaced letters in titles ('Dalmatia F ilm F estival'), pre-2023 amounts ambiguously denominated. Pass A surveys every amount string and flags suspects. Pass B re-reads each suspect against the raw_text neighbourhood and either repairs the amount or stamps it `needs_review` for human inspection.
passes.output: Pass A: 116 suspects · Pass B: 37 repaired + 80 needs_review

prompt_excerpt.caption: Repair-decision tags used in _amount_repair_report.md
prompt_excerpt.body:
tag             meaning
--------------- ---------------------------------------------------------
repaired        amount was confidently fixed from a neighbouring string
needs_review    amount could not be fixed unambiguously — flagged for human
croatian_std    repair confidence track: Croatian decimal convention applied
high / medium / low   confidence of the neighbourhood read

io_example.caption: rezultati komplementarne 2021.pdf — Pass B in action
io_example.expected:
Pass A flags row 4 as suspect: current=0.0 ('0.000,00').
Pass B should inspect the raw_text and either repair or mark needs_review.
io_example.received:
[repaired]    rn=4   Autonomni kulturni centar    old=0.0 → new=20000.0 (croatian_std, high, €2,654)
[repaired]    rn=9   Dalmatia Film Festival       old=0.0 → new=10000.0 (croatian_std, high, €1,327)
[repaired]    rn=10  Festival mediteranskog filma old=0.0 → new=10000.0 (croatian_std, high, €1,327)
[needs_review] rn=22 Mladi mladima — poticanje…   current=0.0 ('0.000,00')   // amount illegible in PDF

passes.title: Director / writer / original-author backfill
passes.what: Most early results_table records had blank director / writer / original_author fields because pre-2014 PDFs listed those names in narrative paragraphs adjacent to the table, not as columns. The collect script slices each record into a per-record JSON batch containing the rows and the full raw_text, dispatches it to a Claude subagent with a tightly-scoped prompt, and the subagent emits exactly one decision per row. Apply merges those decisions back into master.json.
passes.input: 418 per-record batches; each carries rows + raw_text
passes.output: 418 decision JSON files; merged into master.json by _director_apply.py

prompt_excerpt.caption: dataset/_director_prompt.md — column-name candidates the subagent searches raw_text for
prompt_excerpt.body:
Extract from adjacent columns when present:

- director column candidates:
    REDATELJ · REDATELJ/ICA · Redatelj/-ica · Redateljica · Režija
- writer column candidates:
    SCENARIST/ICA · Scenarist/-ica · Scenaristica · Scenarij
- original-author column candidates:
    AUTOR IZVORNOG PREDLOŠKA · IZVORNI PREDLOŽAK · Prema romanu · prema priči · prema noveli · prema djelu

If a current field is already non-null, prefer returning null for that field unless the PDF clearly shows a better canonical value.
Preserve Croatian diacritics exactly (č ć š ž đ Č Ć Š Ž Đ).

io_example.caption: One row from batch 099840fa — AV proizvodnja 2010.pdf
io_example.received:
{
  "section_idx": 0,
  "row_idx": 7,
  "director":        null,        // not present in raw_text
  "writer":          null,        // ditto
  "original_author": "prema noveli Slavka Mihalića",
  "confidence":      "medium",
  "reasoning":       "raw_text contains 'prema noveli Slavka Mihalića' two lines below the project title."
}

passes.title: Producer-field pollution sweep
passes.what: The production_company and applicant columns sometimes contain pollution that the table extractor copied from adjacent cells: section labels, totals rows, descriptive sentences leaked from project_title or raw_text. A regex pre-classifier emits 196 candidates with a bucket hint (amount_shaped, header_or_category, sentence_like); Claude makes the final drop / keep / replace call.
passes.input: 196 candidate (record, row, field) tuples with current value + bucket hint

prompt_excerpt.caption: dataset/_producer_pollution_prompt.md — decision policy (excerpt)
prompt_excerpt.body:
bucket: "amount_shaped"      → almost always drop. Amounts never belong in a producer field.

bucket: "header_or_category":
  - "PRODUCENT" literal                       → drop (column header)
  - "filmski festivali...", "izdavaštvo..."   → drop (komplementarne sub-programme labels)
  - "Produkcija ...", "Projekt ..." + name    → keep
  - "Dugometra*", "Animirani" standalone      → drop (category header)

bucket: "sentence_like":
  - Starts with "Sudjelovanje", "Predstavljanje", "U produkciji" → drop (project description leaked from title)
  - Contains unambiguous "Producent: X" or "u produkciji X-a"    → replace with X

io_example.caption: Three real candidates, three verdicts
io_example.expected: Each candidate gets exactly one of drop / keep / replace, with reasoning.
io_example.received:
current_value="PRODUCENT"                       bucket=header_or_category → drop     reasoning="column header leaked into producer cell"
current_value="Sudjelovanje filma U Šumi na…" bucket=sentence_like       → drop     reasoning="project description, not a producer"
current_value="Produkcija Živa d.o.o."          bucket=header_or_category → keep     reasoning="legitimate producer despite matching 'Produkcija' prefix"

passes.title: Producer cluster + canonical
passes.what: After Pass 7 stripped pollution, ~700 unique producer-name strings remained — but many were OCR variants of the same legal entity: 'Nukleus film d. o. o.', 'Nukleus Film d.o.o.', 'NUKLEUS FILM d.o.o.'. A diacritic-stripped, suffix-stripped, alphanum-only normaliser collapsed them into 240 clusters. Claude then picks a single canonical name per cluster — preferring the d.o.o. suffix, mixed case, no spurious spaces — and can split a cluster if the normaliser over-collapsed two distinct entities into one bucket.
passes.input: 240 clusters of variant strings, with occurrence counts
passes.output: Per cluster: canonical_name + per-member mapping (with optional owner_split)

prompt_excerpt.caption: dataset/_producer_cluster_prompt.md — canonical-name selection rules
prompt_excerpt.body:
1. Prefer the form with d.o.o. / d.d. / j.d.o.o. suffix if any variant has it.
   Example: 'Kinorama d.o.o.' over 'Kinorama' or 'KINORAMA'.
2. Prefer normal mixed-case over ALL CAPS or lowercase.
   Example: 'Restart' over 'RESTART'.
3. Drop spurious spaces in the legal suffix: 'Kinorama d .o.o.' → 'Kinorama d.o.o.'.
4. Strip ' / <owner-name>' suffix: 'Kinorama d.o.o. / Lado Skorin' →
   canonical 'Kinorama d.o.o.', owner 'Lado Skorin' as owner_split.
5. Single-letter typos / OCR splits: 'Nukleus film d. o. o.', 'Nukleus film d.o.o',
   'Nukleus Film d.o.o.' → canonical 'Nukleus Film d.o.o.'.
6. Resolve case to Title Case proper-noun casing.

io_example.caption: One real cluster decision

passes.title: URL-less dedup audit (Codex)
passes.engine: normalize_pass.py (deterministic twin-match plan) → codex_prompt.md (Codex CLI verifies) → apply
passes.what: 18 results_table records had no source.source_url. Most turned out to be duplicates of urlful records (the missing-results-backfill extractor sometimes re-extracted from a renamed copy of a PDF already in the corpus). A deterministic pre-pass finds twin rows by (normTitle, approved_amount, program_type) and proposes drop_row / flag_row decisions per row. Codex CLI then verifies the proposals against the raw_text of both sides and writes a final decision JSON.
passes.input: 18 urlless docs + the 524 urlful docs they might be duplicates of
passes.output: Per-doc classification: drop_doc | partial | flag_doc · per-row: drop_row | flag_row

prompt_excerpt.caption: dash/havc/codex_prompt.md — verification task (excerpt)
prompt_excerpt.body:
For each urlless doc, verify per-row decisions:

1. For each drop_row: confirm the twin is genuine — same project, same round,
   same funding decision (not just a coincidental amount/title collision
   across different rounds).
2. For each flag_row: confirm no twin was missed due to spelling variants
   (diacritics encoded as `_`, abbreviated names, rounding of amounts, mojibake).
   If you find a missed twin, change the row to drop_row and add the twin sha
   to matched_twins.

Be conservative: when in doubt, keep flag_row rather than risk dropping a
legitimate funding decision.

io_example.caption: Two real per-doc verdicts from normalize-plan.md
io_example.expected: Per-doc: drop_doc (all rows duplicate), partial (some rows duplicate), or flag_doc (no rows duplicate).
io_example.received:
drop_doc    Rezultati JP koprodukcije rok 3110.pdf                       3/3 rows have exact twins in urlful 73ba096f → drop all three rows.
flag_doc    FESTIVALI I KAT_DUGI 2014_web.pdf                              0/15 rows have twins → keep all 15, stamp source_url_missing=true.
partial     30_AV proizvodnja – kratkometražni igrani – 1. ROK 07.04.2020. 18/33 rows duplicate → drop those 18, keep the other 15 as flag_row.

intro.text: If you ignore implementation details, the project did four things: sort documents, extract structure, detect bad rows/amounts, and repeatedly repair with auditable evidence.

body.text: Each PDF was classified before any paid extraction call. This prevented random routing and made later audits interpretable.
Dropped rows, repaired amounts, and unresolved edge cases were written into reports, not hidden in code comments.
Instead of one giant rewrite, the dataset was corrected pass-by-pass: backfill, amount triage, people, producer normalization, URL-less dedup.

intro.text: The excerpts below are sanitized summaries from assistant-session history plus local artifacts. They show intent and concrete changes without leaking sensitive metadata.

summary.text: The initial constraint was parity over all published HAVC PDFs, with deterministic routing before extraction.

problem.text: Mixed PDF types (results, narratives, admin docs) made naive one-pass extraction noisy.

decision.text: Route by classifier first, then call specialized extractors only where needed.

result.text: A stable front door for all later passes and clearer failure attribution.

excerpt_compact.caption: Sanitized excerpt
excerpt_compact.body:
Goal: "100% parity from PDFs, repeatable when new files arrive."
Action: Build classifier -> extractor routing instead of one generic parser.

excerpt_more.caption: What changed next
excerpt_more.body: After routing, extraction logic split into table vs narrative tools, which made missing-table backfill possible later.

summary.text: Post-extraction scans found cases where data existed in PDFs but was not captured on the first route.

problem.text: Narrative-classified files sometimes still contained decision tables.

decision.text: Run a dedicated backfill pass and tag extracted records by extractor channel.

result.text: Missing decisions were recovered without rewriting earlier passes.

excerpt_compact.caption: Sanitized excerpt
excerpt_compact.body:
Intent: "If a table exists anywhere in the PDF, it must be represented."
Action: Add missing-results channel and re-run only flagged files.

excerpt_more.caption: Audit behavior
excerpt_more.body: Backfilled rows stay traceable via source.extractor so later normalization can separate planned vs recovered extraction.

summary.text: After coverage improved, quality passes removed fake rows and investigated suspicious amount strings.

problem.text: Header fragments and OCR noise leaked into project rows and amounts.

decision.text: Use deterministic reason codes for bogus drops, then triage suspect amounts with neighborhood checks.

result.text: Rows were either dropped with reason codes or retained with explicit `needs_review` status.

excerpt_compact.caption: Sanitized excerpt
excerpt_compact.body:
Observation: "Stavka/address/category headers are being treated as projects."
Action: Add reason-coded drop pass before downstream analytics.

excerpt_more.caption: Repair discipline
excerpt_more.body: When repair confidence was low, rows were preserved and flagged instead of force-corrected.

summary.text: Identity fields were inconsistent, so dedicated passes filled missing creators and normalized producer names.

problem.text: Director/writer/original-author gaps and producer spelling variants reduced query quality.

decision.text: Dispatch per-record people batches, then cluster producer variants and map to canonical names.

result.text: Large portions of people fields were filled, and producer/applicant values became more stable.

excerpt_compact.caption: Sanitized excerpt
excerpt_compact.body:
Intent: "Same company should not appear as four OCR variants."
Action: Cluster + canonical mapping with explicit audit output.

excerpt_more.caption: Back-and-forth pattern
excerpt_more.body: Collect -> dispatch -> apply -> verify loops kept each transformation scoped and reversible.

summary.text: Final normalization targeted URL-less documents and duplicate row collisions before dashboard delivery.

problem.text: Some records had no source URL and partially duplicated URL-backed rows.

decision.text: Build deterministic twin plan, then verify with Codex audit before applying row-level decisions.

result.text: Duplicates were dropped conservatively; unresolved rows were kept but flagged.

excerpt_compact.caption: Sanitized excerpt
excerpt_compact.body:
Rule: "When in doubt, keep and flag, do not drop."
Action: Verified row-level matches before any deletion decision.

excerpt_more.caption: Delivery constraint
excerpt_more.body: This pass balanced data cleanliness against traceability: every drop decision stayed attributable to a plan + audit artifact.

eras.label: Era 4
eras.title: Verification, curation, and recurring project identity

system.input: 12,845 extracted result rows plus earlier parity and audit evidence
process: deterministic cleanup and stable row IDs
structured Haiku row adjudication with cached recovery
explicit funding statuses and idempotent validation
system.output: 9,543 result rows · 9,542 verified awards · 1 explicit non-award · 0 unresolved

what.text: The final curation layer stopped treating every extracted row as an award. Deterministic rules removed known artifacts and recovered shifted fields; Haiku reviewed ambiguous rows with the surrounding table and source text; direct PDF checks were recorded as explicit corrections. Annual editions were linked into stable project families while their original edition titles remained available in timelines.

why_good.text: Title shape alone never decides validity. Numeric, quoted, short, and unusual creative titles remain valid when the source supports them.
Only verified awards enter totals and the default registry. Explicit non-awards remain available for the unfunded-project view.

why_good: Cached decisions and byte-idempotent output make the final pass repeatable without paying for completed reviews again.
Project families solve annual-edition fragmentation without erasing the published title of each edition.
why_limited: New HAVC layouts can still require a narrow source correction or classifier rule.
Missing reviews depend on model access, although completed decisions and recovered sessions remain cached.
Family overrides are intentionally conservative; related but distinct programmes remain separate.

artifacts.note: Deterministic cleanup, structured review, family assignment, and validation
Versioned corrections verified directly against original PDFs
Final status totals, model-call receipts, and validation result

rows.era4: Curated result rows; uncertain rows excluded
Preserved and linked to verified families
Stable family IDs; edition titles preserved
Row decision → evidence → cache → final validation
